Rashi on Shabbat 23a:10:1.hebrew: חצר שיש לה ב' פתחים - שיש לבית ב' פתחים פתוחים לחצר, צריכ' שתי נרות — נר לכל פתח, כדמפ' טעמא: משום חשדא, שהרואה יהא סבור שהבית חלוק והרי הוא של שני בני אדם, ויאמרו: האחד אינו מקיים מצות נר:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:10:1.english: A courtyard that has two entrances - [In a case] where a house has two entrances open to the courtyard, [it] requires two lamps — one lamp for each entrance — as [the Gemara] explains the reason: because of suspicion, for an onlooker will assume that the house is divided and belongs to two people, and they will say: "One [of them] does not fulfill the mitzvah of the lamp."

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:10:2.english: From two directions - One [entrance] in the north and one in the east.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:10:3.english: The suspicion of the world - People of another city who pass by there in the street.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:10:4.english: Even from one direction as well - They assume that the house is divided from within.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:10:5.english: And if [it is] the suspicion of the residents of the town - For they know that it is not divided.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:11:1.hebrew: לסוף שדהו - בגמר קצירו, כדכתי': "לא תכלה" — משמע בשעת כילוי, ולא שיקצה אותה קודם לכן:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:11:1.english: At the end of his field - At the completion of its reaping, as it is written: “You shall not wholly reap” — [which] implies at the time of completion, and not that he should designate it prior to that.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:11:2.english: Due to causing the poor to be idle - And [the Gemara] explains all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:11:3.hebrew: שעה פנויה - שאין עניים אצלו, ויאמר לקרובו עני: מהר וטול כאן עד שלא יבאו אחרים. אבל עכשיו שמניחה בגמר קציר השד', העניים רואין ובאין:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:11:3.english: An unoccupied time - [A time] when there are no poor people with him, and he would say to his poor relative: "Hurry and take [from] here before others arrive." But now that he leaves it at the completion of harvesting the field, the poor people see and come.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:1:1.hebrew: עששית - כלי גדול של זכוכית, בלעז: לנטרנ"א:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:1:1.english: A lantern - A large glass vessel, in Old French: lanterne.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:1:2.english: Burning - That he kindled it for the mitzvah of Hanukkah on Shabbat eve.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:1:3.english: And lights it - For the mitzvah of the night.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:2:1.hebrew: היו באותו הנס - שגזרו יוונים על כל בתולות הנשואות להיבעל לטפסר תחלה, ועל יד אשה נעשה הנס:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:2:1.english: [They] were in that miracle - For the Greeks decreed that all virgins about to be married must have intercourse with the commander first, and the miracle was performed through a woman.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:3:2.english: After I married - And [there were] times when I was a guest to study Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:3:4.english: Inside my house - In my house.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:4:1.english: Its light is drawn out - It does not burn out as quickly as olive oil.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:4:2.english: Its light is clear - Clear and bright.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:5:1.hebrew: לגבל - מצאתי בתשוב' הגאוני' שמעשנין כלי זכוכית בעשן שמן זית עד שמשחיר, וגורר השחרורי', ונותן בו שמן קימעא, ומגבל בו, ומייבשו בחמה, וממחה אותו לתוך הדיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:5:1.english: To knead - I found in a responsum of the Geonim that one smokes a glass vessel with the smoke of olive oil until it blackens, scrapes off the soot, puts a little oil into it, kneads [it] with it, dries it in the sun, and dissolves it into the ink.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:5:2.english: To smoke - [This] is also as I explained.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:5:4.hebrew: קטף - פרוניי"ל של יער, כמו שאנו עושים משל שרף:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:5:4.english: Kataf - [The] wild plum tree [blackthorn; Old French: prunelier] of the forest, as we make [ink] from sap.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:6:1.hebrew: הרואה - העובר בשוק ורואה באחד החצרות דולק. ומצאתי בשם רבינו יצחק בן יהודה, שאמר משם רבינו יעקב, דלא הוזקקה ברכה זו אלא למי שלא הדליק בביתו עדיין, או ליושב בספינ':
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:6:1.english: One who sees - One who passes through the marketplace and sees [a lamp] burning in one of the courtyards. And I found in the name of Rabbeinu Yitzchak ben Yehuda, who said in the name of Rabbeinu Yaakov, that this blessing was instituted only for one who has not yet lit in his home, or for one who is aboard a ship.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:6:2.hebrew: הרואה מברך שתים - שעשה נסים ושהחיינו, שאין עליו לברך להדליק, דהא לא אדליק איהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:6:2.english: One who sees recites two [blessings] - [The blessings] 'Who performed miracles' and 'Who has kept us alive,' for he is not obligated to recite [the blessing] 'to kindle,' since he did not kindle [it] himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:6:3.hebrew: מאי ממעט - המדליק בשאר ימים, איזו מן השלש ממעט:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:6:3.english: What does he omit - [As for] the one who lights on the other days, which of the three [blessings] does he omit?

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:6:4.hebrew: כל יומי איתיה - שהרי כל שמנה הדליקו מן הפך, אבל זמן — משהגיענו להתחלת זמן, הגיענו:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:6:4.english: [The miracle] is [present] all days - For all eight [days] they lit from the cruse [of oil]; but [as for the blessing of] time — once He has brought us to the beginning of the time, He has brought us [to this time].

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:7:1.hebrew: היכן צונו - הא לאו דאורייתא היא, אלא מדבריהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:7:1.english: Where did He command us - For it is not from the Torah, but rather from their words [of the Sages].

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:7:2.english: From “You shall not turn aside” - [The verse continues:] “From the matter that they will tell you,” etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:1.english: One may make an eiruv with it - Eiruvei chatzerot [the joining of courtyards] and [eruvei] techumin [the joining of Shabbat boundaries].

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:2.hebrew: משתתפין בו - במבוי. דאי בעי, מפקר לנכסיה והוה עני וחזי ליה, כדתנן: מאכילין את העניים דמאי. הלכך, חשוב דידיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:2.english: One may establish a shituf with it - In an alleyway. For if he wished, he could renounce ownership of his property and become poor, and it would be fit for him, as we learned in a mishna: "We may feed the poor demai." Therefore, it is considered his [own food].

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:3.english: And one recites a blessing over it - [The blessing of] HaMotzi.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:4.english: And one recites a zimmun over it - The blessing of the zimmun.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:5.hebrew: ומפריש אותו - אדם שהוא ערום, כלומר, דלא צריך לברוכי עליה בהפרשתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:5.english: And one separates it - A person who is naked [may separate it] — that is to say, that one does not need to recite a blessing over it upon its separation.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:6.hebrew: והיה מחניך קדוש - ולא יראה בך ערות דבר — אפילו דבור דהזכרת השם, לא יראה בך ערות דבר:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:6.english: And your camp shall be holy - [The verse continues:] “That He see no unseemly thing in you” — even [for] speech involving the mention of the [Divine] Name, no unseemly thing [i.e., nakedness] may be seen in you.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:7.english: A definite [ordinance] of the Sages - Such as the Hanukkah light.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:8:8.english: An uncertain [matter] of Rabbinic origin - Such as demai, whose separation [of tithes] is only due to doubt.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:9:1.english: And it requires a blessing - The sanctification of the day.

Rashi on Shabbat 23a:9:2.hebrew: רבא אמר - ספק דדבריהם בעי ברכה, ודמאי אפילו ספק לא הוי, אלא חומרא בעלמא — דרוב עמי הארץ מעשרין:
Rashi on Shabbat 23a:9:2.english: Rava said - [A matter of] Rabbinic uncertainty requires a blessing, and demai is not even an uncertainty, but merely a stringency — for most of the common folk [amei ha'aretz] tithe.

Tosafot on Shabbat 23a:1:1.hebrew: מכבה ומגביהה ומניחה וחוזר ומדליק מיבעי ליה - וא"ת: אמאי מכבה וחוזר ומדליק? בהגבהה סגי, כיון דהנחה עושה מצוה — דאטו מי גרע דלוקה ועומדת מהדליקה חש"ו? וי"ל: דמיירי שהדליקה מתחלתה לצורך שבת, ולכך גרע מהדליקה חש"ו — דהתם, שמדליקה בעתה, ניכר הדבר שהוא מדליקה לשם חנוכה. ריב"א:
Tosafot on Shabbat 23a:1:1.english: "It should have [said]: 'One extinguishes it, lifts it, sets it down, and relights it'" - And if you say: Why must he extinguish and relight [it]? Lifting it [and setting it down] should be sufficient, since placing accomplishes the mitzvah — for is [a lamp that is] already burning any worse than [one] kindled by a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor? And one can say: [The Gemara] is dealing with [a case where] he kindled it from the outset for the purpose of Shabbat, and therefore it is worse than [a lamp] kindled by a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor — for there, where he kindles it at its [proper] time, the matter is recognizable that he is kindling it for the sake of Hanukkah. — Riva [Rabbi Isaac ben Asher].

Tosafot on Shabbat 23a:1:2.hebrew: שמע מינה הדלקה עושה מצוה - וא"כ, מותר להדליק מנר לנר. ומכל מקום, כיון שנהגו העולם להחמיר, אין לשנות המנהג:
Tosafot on Shabbat 23a:1:2.english: "Conclude from this [that] lighting accomplishes the mitzvah" - And if so, it is permitted to light from [one] lamp to [another] lamp. And nevertheless, since people are accustomed to be stringent, one should not change the custom.

Tosafot on Shabbat 23a:4:1.hebrew: מריש הוה מהדר מר אמשחא דשומשמי - נראה דאנר חנוכה קאי, ומשום טעמא דמסיק: דנפיש נהוריה טפי. אבל לנר שבת — פשיטא דשמן זית מצוה מן המובחר, לפי שנמשך אחר הפתילה טפי מכולהו, כדמוכח במתניתין, דכולהו מודו ביה דמדליקין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 23a:4:1.english: "At first, the Master would seek sesame oil" - It appears that [this] refers to the Hanukkah lamp, and on account of the reason that [the Gemara] concludes: that its light is greater. But for the Shabbat lamp, it is obvious that olive oil is the choicest [fulfillment of the] mitzvah, because it is drawn into the wick better than all of them, as is proven in the Mishnah, where all agree that one may light with it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 23a:5:1.hebrew: כל השרפים יפים לדיו - פירש בקונטרס: שרף — גומא. ואין נראה לר"ת, דהא דיו אין זה גומא, כדאמרינן בפ"ב דגיטין (דף יט. ושם): בכל כותבין — בדיו, בסם, ובסקרא, ובקומוס; ומפרש בגמרא: קומוס — גומא. ודיו נמי אין זה מי עפצים שרגילין להניח בהן גומא, דהא בברייתא קתני התם: כתבו במי טריא ועפצא — דהיינו עפצים — כשר; משמע דלאו היינו דיו דקתני במתניתין. ועוד, דכשר משמע דיעבד, ובדיו היא עיקר הכתיבה. ועוד, דבפרק כל היד (נדה דף כ. ושם) אמרינן: פלי קורטא דדיותא ובדיק — דהיינו דיו שלנו שהוא קשה, ולא של עפצים; ואין דרך להניח גומא לתוך דיו שלנו. אלא שרף [דהכא] היינו לחלוחית של אילן, כמו שאנו עושין דיו שלנו. וכן יש בנדה בפ"ק (דף י:) גבי בתולה: זו שירפה מצוי וזו אין שירפה מצוי. וכן בפ' כל שעה (פסחים לט. ושם): ירק מר יש לו שרף ופניו מכסיפין, דע"כ ההוא שרף היינו לחלוחית. ועל כן היה פוסל ר"ת ס"ת שאין כותבין בדיו שלנו, דשאר לא מיקרי דיו, כדפי'. ואמרי' בפ' הבונה (לקמן שבת קג:): כתבו שלא בדיו — הרי אלו יגנזו; ומוקמי' לה בהקומץ רבה (מכחות דף לד) בס"ת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 23a:5:1.english: "All saps are good for ink" - Rashi explained: Seraf [means] gum. And this does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Tam, for behold, deyo (ink) is not gum, as we say in the second chapter of Gittin (19a): "One may write with anything: with ink, with sam, with sikra, and with kumos," and the Gemara explains: Kumos is gum. And deyo is also not gallnut water, into which it is customary to put gum, for behold, a baraita teaches there: "[If] one wrote it with mei tarya or afatza" — which is gallnuts — "[it is] valid," which implies that this is not the deyo that is taught in the Mishnah. And furthermore, "[it is] valid" implies [only] after the fact (bedi'avad), whereas with deyo is the primary [form of] writing. And furthermore, in the chapter "Kol HaYad" (Niddah 20a) we say: "He split a piece of dry ink and tested [it]," which refers to our ink, which is hard, and not [ink] of gallnuts; and it is not customary to put gum into our ink. Rather, seraf [here] refers to the sap of a tree, as we make our ink. And so it is in Niddah in the first chapter (10b) regarding a virgin: "This one has her moisture [shirpah] plentiful, and this one does not have her moisture plentiful." And so too in the chapter "Kol Sha'ah" (Pesachim 39a): "A bitter vegetable has sap [seraf] and its surface blanches," where perforce that seraf means moisture. And therefore, Rabbeinu Tam would invalidate a Torah scroll that was not written with our ink, for other [types of ink] are not called deyo, as explained. And we say in the chapter "HaBoneh" (below, Shabbat 103b): "[If] they wrote them not with deyo, behold, they must be stored away"; and we establish it in [the chapter] "HaKometz Rabbah" (Menachot 34b) as referring to a Torah scroll.
